Kings of Macedonia during the dynastic conflicts (294–272 BC)

Table data.Name: Demetrius I "Poliorcetes"
Table data.Succession: Proclaimed king by army in Larissa following Alexander V's assassination; son of the diadochos Antigonus and brother-in-law of Cassander through Phila
Table data.Life details: January/February 336 – 282 (aged 54) Surrendered to Seleucus I Nicator in 285, died of illness in captivity a few years later.

Table data.Name: (1st reign) Pyrrhus of Epirus
Table data.Succession: Usurped throne following joint invasion of Macedonia with Lysimachus and Ptolemy; non-dynastic.
Table data.Life details: c. 319 – 272 (aged 46) Killed at the Battle of Argos.

Table data.Name: Lysimachus
Table data.Succession: Ruled only the eastern half of the kingdom until 284 when he seized the whole of Macedonia; non-dynastic.
Table data.Life details: c. 360 – 281 (aged 79) Killed at the Battle of Corupedium .

Table data.Name: Ptolemy "Ceraunus"
Table data.Succession: Assassinated Seleucus before he entered Macedon and was proclaimed king at Lysimachia ; son of Ptolemy I Soter .
Table data.Life details: c. 319/18 – February 279 (aged approx. 40)  Captured and beheaded by an invading Celtic army .

Table data.Name: Meleager
Table data.Succession: Elected king following the death of Ceraunus; son of Ptolemy I Soter .
Table data.Life details: Unknown Deposed by Macedonians after accusations of inadequacy

Table data.Name: Antipater II "Etesias"
Table data.Succession: Elected king following Meleager's removal; nephew of Cassander
Table data.Life details: Unknown Removed by Sosthenes for failing to lead the army.

Table data.Name: Sosthenes
Table data.Succession: Strategos and de facto king of Macedon, but refused royal title despite election; non-dynastic
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 277 Died of natural causes.

Table data.Name: (1st reign) Antigonus II "Gonatas"
Table data.Succession: Seized Macedonia by the middle of 276 in the chaos  that followed the death of Sosthenes; son of Demetrius I and son-in-law of Seleucus I Nicator
Table data.Life details: 319 – 239 (aged 80) Died of natural causes.

Table data.Name: (2nd reign) Pyrrhus of Epirus
Table data.Succession: Retook Thessaly and the interior of Macedonia, but remained unable to oust Antigonus from the coastal areas
Table data.Life details: c. 319 – 272 (aged 46) Killed at the Battle of Argos .

Group name: Kings of Macedonia from the Antigonid dynasty (272–168 BC)

Table data.Name: (2nd reign) Antigonus II "Gonatas"
Table data.Succession: Son of Demetrius I and son-in-law of Seleucus I Nicator
Table data.Life details: 319 – 239 (aged 80) Died of natural causes.

Table data.Name: Demetrius II
Table data.Succession: Son of Antigonus II
Table data.Life details: c. 275/4 – 229 (aged approx. 45) Defeated in battle by the Dardanians, died shortly after in unknown circumstances.

Table data.Name: Antigonus III "Doson"
Table data.Succession: Chosen by "leading Macedonians" to rule first as regent for Philip and, then later, as king; grandson of Demetrius I and cousin of Demetrius II
Table data.Life details: c. 263 – 221 (aged approx. 42) Suffering from tuberculosis, Antigonus burst a blood vessel following a battle with the Illyrians and died some months later.

Table data.Name: Philip V
Table data.Succession: Son of Demetrius II
Table data.Life details: 239 – 179 (aged 60) Died suddenly of natural causes.

Table data.Name: Perseus I
Table data.Succession: Son of Philip V
Table data.Life details: 212 – 166 (aged 46) Surrendered to Aemilius Paullus following defeat at Pydna and imprisoned at Alba Fucens for the remainder of his life.

Table data.Name: Antipater I

Group name: Murders of minors in France between 2011 and 2020

Table data.Summary: On 4 June 2011 in Pau , murder of Alexandre Junca, a 13-year-old schoolboy by a stranger. His body dismembered by four accomplices.
Table data.Convictions and comments: Mickaël Baehrel is sentenced on 16 June 2016, to life imprisonment by the Pyrénées-Atlantiques Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 6 November 2011 in Bellegarde , Océane Luna, 8 years old, was abducted, raped and murdered by Nicolas Blondiau.
Table data.Convictions and comments: Nicolas Blondiau was sentenced on 17 February 2013, to life imprisonment without parole by the Gard Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 16 November 2011 in Le Chambon-sur-Lignon , Agnès Marin, 13 years old, was raped and murdered by Mathieu Moulinas, 17 years old, a repeat offender.
Table data.Convictions and comments: Mathieu Moulinas was sentenced on 28 June 2013, to life imprisonment by the Haute-Loire Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 27 March 2012, 17-year-old Alexandre Castaldo was shot twice in the neck and incinerated in a forest by four high school friends in Beauvoir-en-Lyons .
Table data.Convictions and comments: Anthony S. was sentenced on 30 May 2013 to 20 years of criminal imprisonment, Yohan L. to 18, Cyril L. to 16, Kévin S. to 15 years by the Seine-Maritime Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 12 May 2013 in Clermont-Ferrand , 5-year-old Fiona Bourgeon, was murdered by her mother Cécile Bourgeon and her partner, Berkane Makhlouf.
Table data.Convictions and comments: Berkane Makhlouf was sentenced on 26 November 2016 to 20 years of criminal imprisonment by the Puy-de-Dôme Assize Court, Cécile Bourgeon was acquitted on 20 February 2019 by the Court of Cassation.

Table data.Summary: On 15 April 2015 in Calais , 9-year-old Chloé Ansel was raped and murdered in a forest, by Zbigniew Huminski, a Polish worker.
Table data.Convictions and comments: Zbigniew Huminski, the perpetrator, committed suicide before his trial on 14 May 2017.

Table data.Summary: On 27 August 2017 in Le Pont-de-Beauvoisin , Maëlys de Araujo, 8 years old, was kidnapped during a wedding ceremony and then killed by Nordahl Lelandais .
Table data.Convictions and comments: Nordahl Lelandais was sentenced to life imprisonment with a 22-year security term by the Isère Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 25 April 2018 in Wambrechies , kidnapping and sequestration, rape followed by murder of 13-year-old Angélique Six by David Ramault.
Table data.Convictions and comments: David Ramault was sentenced to life imprisonment with a 25-year security period by the Northern Assize Court.

Table data.Summary: On 25 October 2019 in Creil , Shaïna Hansye, 15, already the victim of a gang rape in August 2017, was stabbed and burned alive by a 17-year-old boy with whom she was pregnant.
Table data.Convictions and comments: X was sentenced to 18 years of criminal imprisonment by the Oise juvenile court.

Group name: Argentine main dishes

Table data.Name: Asado
Table data.Description: a range of barbecue techniques usually consisting of beef alongside various other meats, which are cooked on a grill, or open fire. It is considered a national dish.

Table data.Name: Churrasco
Table data.Description: any cut of beef that is sliced slightly thin as a steak and grilled over hot coals or on a very hot skillet.

Table data.Name: Humita
Table data.Description: prepared with fresh corn , sautéed onions and some spices, depending on the region or taste. The dough is wrapped in corn husks and boiled.

Table data.Name: Locro
Table data.Description: a stew of squash, meat, and hominy

Table data.Name: Matambre
Table data.Description: a roulade of flank steak and vegetables usually cut in thick slices and served cold.

Table data.Name: Milanesas
Table data.Description: a thin, breaded and deep fried or baked slice of beef, chicken, or sometimes pork, and even eggplants or soy.

Table data.Name: Pascualina
Table data.Description: a spinach and/or chard pie originally from Italy, very similar to the Greek spanakopita

Table data.Name: Polenta
Table data.Description: cornmeal boiled into a porridge, usually served with cheese and sometimes tomato sauce

Table data.Name: Pollo al disco
Table data.Description: a stew of chicken and vegetables cooked in a deep round dish over an open fire

Table data.Name: Revuelto Gramajo
Table data.Description: A common Argentine breakfast dish consisting of fried julienne potatoes, eggs, cheese and vegetables.

Table data.Name: Sorrentinos
Table data.Description: A type of ravioli created in Mar del Plata by immigrants from Sorrento , Italy

Table data.Name: Vitel toné
Table data.Description: cold, sliced veal covered with a creamy, mayonnaise-like sauce that has been flavored with tuna . It is considered a traditional Christmas dish .

Traditional dishes and beverages from East Prussia

Table data.Name: Bärenfang
Table data.Description: A German honey -flavoured liqueur based on vodka. It is usually called Bärenjäger in English-speaking countries also Meschkinnes (wild like a bear in Old Prussian).

Table data.Name: Beetenbartsch
Table data.Description: A beetroot-based soup served with sour cream ( Schmand ) and beef (originally from Ukraine ) Similar to Borscht .

Table data.Name: Kuttelsuppe
Table data.Description: A lightly bound soup from tripe , usually with acidified vinegar that mentions regional spots, which is common in variants in numerous countries. Known as Fleck in East Prussia.

Table data.Name: Königsberger Klopse
Table data.Description: Meatballs served in a slightly sweet/sour white cream sauce with capers and eaten with potatoes.

Table data.Name: Königsberger Marzipan
Table data.Description: Special kind of marzipan browned under the broiler, made in Königsberg since 1555, flavoured with rose water.

Table data.Name: Kopskiekelwein
Table data.Description: A wine made from either blackcurrants or redcurrants, and usually fermented with Burgundy yeast.

Table data.Name: Pillkaller Machandel
Table data.Description: A clear liqueur known as Korn that is served in a shot glass with liver sausage and mustard.

Table data.Name: Schwarzsauer
Table data.Description: A type of blood soup with various spices cooked in vinegar-water.

Table data.Name: Spirgel
Table data.Description: The East Prussian name for fried bacon or pork belly as well as for a simple dish of diced pancetta or pork belly and onions served with boiled potatoes.

Table data.Name: Tilsiter cheese
Table data.Description: A light yellow semi-hard rind-ripened cheese, created in the mid-19th century by Prussian-Swiss settlers, the Westphal family, from the Emmental valley.

Group name: Traditional dishes from Schleswig-Holstein, Germany

Table data.Name: Buttermilchsuppe
Table data.Description: Buttermilk soup with flour dumplings

Table data.Name: Gruenkohlgericht
Table data.Description: Cooked kale usually served with potatoes and Kasseler or other foods.

Table data.Name: Kieler Sprotten
Table data.Description: Smoked Baltic sprats .

Table data.Name: Labskaus
Table data.Description: A dish made from corned beef , herring, mashed potatoes, and beetroot, served with a fried egg and a pickled cucumber.

Table data.Name: Mehlbeutel
Table data.Description: A large flour dumpling served with bacon and a sweet sauce.

Table data.Name: Schnüüsch
Table data.Description: A stew made of ham, potatoes and vegetables cooked in roux .

Table data.Name: Schwarzsauer
Table data.Description: A sort of black pudding made with vinegar.

Table data.Name: Snuten un Poten
Table data.Description: Cured pig snouts and trotters that are cooked in vinegar together with several spices. Traditionally served with sauerkraut , erbspüree, and hot mustard .

Group name: Traditional dishes from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern

Table data.Name: Mecklenburger Rippenbraten
Table data.Description: Rib roast, made from belly of pork including meat of the upper rib, stuffed with Boskoop apples, prunes, cinnamon, rum and zwieback, usually served with Klöße and red cabbage.

Table data.Name: Tüffel un Plum
Table data.Description: A potato stew made with smoked ham, prunes, potatoes and spiced with clove and bay leaves.

Table data.Name: Fliederbeersuppe
Table data.Description: Dessert soup made from elderberry, served with semolina dumplings

Table data.Name: Sahnehering

Table data.Description: A soup made from pickled cucumbers, pearl barley, and pork or beef kidneys

Table data.Name: Shchi
Table data.Description: A cabbage soup.  Also can be based on sauerkraut .  Kislye Shchi (sour shchi) despite its name is a fizzy beverage similar to kvass , usually with honey.

Table data.Name: Borscht
Table data.Description: It is traditionally made from meat or bone stock, sautéed vegetables, and beet sour (i.e., fermented beetroot juice). Depending on the recipe, some of these components may be omitted or substituted.

Table data.Name: Svekolnik
Table data.Description: Cold borscht involves use of dairy products and halves of boiled eggs.

Table data.Name: Solyanka
Table data.Description: A thick, spicy and sour soup that contains meat and pickled cucumbers

Table data.Name: Fish Solyanka
Table data.Description: Variation of solyanka replacing meat with fish.

Table data.Name: Shchavel soup (green shchi)

Table data.Name: Ukha

Table data.Details: Markowski was Vader's original drummer. He was fired after just a few months following a poor rehearsal.

Table data.Name: Adam Skwarek
Table data.Details: Skwarek replaced Markowski in the band. He played at one rehearsal, before being fired for being too controlling.

Table data.Name: Robert Bielak

Table data.Name: Jacek Mehring

Group name: Roman emperors of the Tetrarchy during the Dominate period (293–324)

Table data.Name: Diocletian "Jovius" Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus
Table data.Reign: 20 November 284 – 1 May 305 (20 years, 5 months and 11 days) Whole ; then East
Table data.Succession: Commander of the imperial bodyguard, acclaimed by the army after death of Numerian , and proceeded to defeat Numerian's brother, Carinus , in battle
Table data.Life details: 22 December c. 243 – 3 December c. 311 (aged approx. 68) Began the last great persecution of Christianity. First emperor to voluntarily abdicate. Died in unclear circumstances, possibly suicide

Table data.Name: Maximian "Herculius" Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus
Table data.Reign: 1 April 286  – 1 May 305 (19 years and 1 month; West ) November 306 – 11 November 308 (2 years; Italy )
Table data.Succession: Elevated by Diocletian, ruled the western provinces
Table data.Life details: c. 250 – c. July 310 (aged approx. 60) Abdicated with Diocletian, later trying to regain power with, and then from, Maxentius , before being probably killed on orders of Constantine I

Table data.Name: Galerius Gaius Galerius Valerius Maximianus
Table data.Succession: Elevated to caesar in 293 by Diocletian, succeeded as eastern augustus upon Diocletian's abdication
Table data.Life details: c. 258 – May 311 (aged approx. 53) Died of natural causes

Table data.Name: Constantius I "Chlorus" Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius
Table data.Reign: 1 May 305 – 25 July 306 (1 year, 2 months and 24 days; West )
Table data.Succession: Maximian's relation by marriage, elevated to caesar in 293 by Diocletian, succeeded as western augustus upon Maximian's abdication
Table data.Life details: 31 March c. 250 – 25 July 306 (aged approx. 56) Died of natural causes

Table data.Name: Severus II Flavius Valerius Severus
Table data.Succession: Elevated to caesar in 305 by Maximian, promoted to western augustus by Galerius upon Constantius I's death
Table data.Life details: Unknown – September 307 Surrendered to Maximian and Maxentius, later murdered or forced to commit suicide

Table data.Name: Domitius Alexander  Lucius Domitius Alexander (#)
Table data.Succession: Usurped power against Maxentius in the Diocese of Africa and Sardinia. Possibly allied whimself with Constantine I
Table data.Life details: Unknown – c. 310 Defeated and executed by Maxentius.

Table data.Name: Maxentius Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius
Table data.Succession: Son of Maximian and son-in-law of Galerius, seized power in Italy with support of the Praetorian Guard and his father after being passed over in the succession. Not recognized by the other emperors
Table data.Life details: c. 283 – 28 October 312 (aged approx. 29) Died at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge , against Constantine I

Table data.Name: Licinius Valerius Licinianus Licinius
Table data.Reign: 11 November 308 – 19 September 324 (15 years, 10 months and 8 days) West ; then East
Table data.Succession: Elevated by Galerius to replace Severus, in opposition to Maxentius. Defeated Maximinus Daza in a civil war to become sole emperor of the East in 313
Table data.Life details: c. 265 – early 325 (aged approx. 60) Defeated, deposed and put to death by Constantine I

Table data.Name: Maximinus II "Daza" Galerius Valerius Maximinus
Table data.Succession: Nephew of Galerius, elevated to caesar by Galerius in 305, and acclaimed as augustus by his troops in 310
Table data.Life details: 20 November c. 270 – c. July 313 (aged approx. 42) Defeated in civil war against Licinius , died shortly afterwards

Table data.Name: Valerius Valens  Aurelius Valerius Valens
Table data.Succession: Frontier commander in Dacia , elevated by Licinius in opposition to Constantine I
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 317 Executed in the lead-up to a peace settlement between Licinius and Constantine

Table data.Name: Martinian  Mar. Martinianus
Table data.Succession: A senior bureaucrat, elevated by Licinius in opposition to Constantine I
Table data.Life details: Unknown – Spring 325 Deposed by Constantine and banished to Cappadocia , later executed

Group name: Last Western Roman emperors of the Dominate period (455–476)

Table data.Name: Petronius Maximus
Table data.Succession: General and civil official, murdered Valentinian III and married his widow, Licinia Eudoxia
Table data.Life details: c. 397 – 31 May 455 Killed by a mob while fleeing during the Vandalic sack of Rome

Table data.Name: Avitus Eparchius Avitus
Table data.Reign: 9 July 455 – 17 October 456 (1 year, 3 months and 8 days)
Table data.Succession: General; proclaimed emperor by the Visigoths and Gallo-Romans after the death of Petronius Maximus
Table data.Life details: Late 4th century – 456/457 Defeated and deposed by the magister militum Ricimer , became a bishop. Died shortly after of either natural causes, strangulation, or being starved to death

Table data.Name: Majorian Julius Valerius Majorianus
Table data.Reign: 28 December 457 – 2 August 461 (3 years, 7 months and 5 days)
Table data.Succession: General; proclaimed by the army, backed by Ricimer
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 7 August 461 Reconquered Gaul, Hispania and Dalmatia. Deposed and executed by Ricimer

Table data.Name: Libius Severus ( Severus III )
Table data.Reign: 19 November 461 – 14 November 465 (3 years, 11 months and 26 days)
Table data.Succession: Proclaimed emperor by Ricimer
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 14 November 465 Died of natural causes

Table data.Name: Anthemius Procopius Anthemius
Table data.Reign: 12 April 467 – 11 July 472 (5 years, 2 months and 29 days)
Table data.Succession: General; great-grandson of Procopius , a cousin of Julian, and husband of Marcia Euphemia , a daughter of Marcian. Proclaimed western emperor by Leo I
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 11 July 472 The last effective emperor of the West. Murdered by Gundobad after a civil war with Ricimer

Table data.Name: Olybrius Anicius Olybrius
Table data.Succession: Husband of Placidia , a daughter of Valentinian III. Proclaimed emperor by Ricimer
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 2 November 472 Died of dropsy

Table data.Name: Glycerius
Table data.Reign: 3/5 March 473 – 24 June 474 (1 year, 3 months and 19/21 days)
Table data.Succession: General; proclaimed emperor by Gundobad
Table data.Life details: Unknown lifespan Deposed by Julius Nepos and made a bishop, subsequent fate unknown

Table data.Name: Julius Nepos
Table data.Reign: 24 June 474 – 28 August 475 (1 year, 2 months and 4 days) August 475 – 9 May 480 (4 years and 8 months, in Dalmatia )
Table data.Succession: General; married to a relative of Verina , the wife of the eastern emperor Leo I . Installed as western emperor by Leo
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 9 May 480 Fled to Dalmatia in the face of an attack by his magister militum Orestes . Continued to claim to be emperor in exile. Murdered by his retainers

Table data.Name: Romulus "Augustulus" Romulus Augustus
Table data.Succession: Proclaimed emperor by his father, the magister militum Orestes
Table data.Life details: Roughly 465 – after 507/511? The last western emperor. Deposed by the Germanic general Odoacer and retired. Possibly alive as late as 507 or 511; fate unknown

Group name: Roman emperors of the Leonid dynasty

Table data.Name: Leo I "the Thracian"
Table data.Reign: 7 February 457 – 18 January 474 (16 years, 11 months and 11 days)
Table data.Succession: Low-ranking army officer; chosen by the magister militum Aspar to succeed Marcian
Table data.Life details: 400/401 – 18 January 474 (aged 73) First emperor to be crowned by the Patriarch of Constantinople . Died of dysentery

Table data.Name: Leo II "the Younger"
Table data.Succession: Grandson of Leo I and son of Zeno; co-emperor since 17 November 473
Table data.Life details: 467 – November 474 (aged 7) Youngest emperor at the time of his death. Died of illness

Table data.Name: Zeno
Table data.Succession: Husband of Ariadne , a daughter of Leo I, and father of Leo II. Crowned senior co-emperor with the approval of the Senate
Table data.Life details: 425 – 9 April 491 (aged 65) Fled to Isauria in the face of a Revolt led by his mother-in-law Verina & Basiliscus .

Table data.Name: Basiliscus
Table data.Reign: 9 January 475 – August 476 (1 year and 7 months) with Marcus (475–476)
Table data.Succession: Brother of Verina , the wife of Leo I. Proclaimed emperor by his sister in opposition to Zeno and seized Constantinople
Table data.Life details: Unknown – 476/477 Deposed by Zeno upon his return to Constantinople; imprisoned in a dried-up reservoir and starved to death

Table data.Name: Zeno ( second reign )
Table data.Succession: Retook the throne with the help of general Illus
Table data.Life details: 425 – 9 April 491 (aged 65) Saw the end of the Western Roman Empire . Died of dysentery or epilepsy

Table data.Name: Anastasius I "Dicorus"
Table data.Reign: 11 April 491 – 9 July 518 (27 years, 2 months and 28 days)
Table data.Succession: Government official; chosen by Ariadne, whom he married, to succeed Zeno
Table data.Life details: 430/431 – 9 July 518 (aged 88) Oldest emperor at the time of his death. Died of natural causes

Group name: Roman emperors of the Heraclian dynasty

Table data.Name: Heraclius Ἡράκλειος
Table data.Reign: 5 October 610 – 11 February 641 (30 years, 4 months and 6 days)
Table data.Succession: Son of Heraclius the Elder , the exarch of Carthage . Led a revolt against Phocas
Table data.Life details: 574/575 – 11 February 641 (aged 66) Ended the Persian Wars , but suffered the loss of the Levant to the Muslims. Died of natural causes

Table data.Name: Heraclius Constantine ( Constantine III )  Heraclius Constantinus Ἡράκλειος Κωνσταντῖνος
Table data.Succession: Son of Heraclius; co-emperor since 22 January 613
Table data.Life details: 3 May 612 – 25 May 641 (aged 29) Died of tuberculosis

Table data.Name: Heraclonas Heraclius , Ἡράκλειος
Table data.Reign: 25 May – 5 November (?) 641 (5 months and 11 days) with his brother Tiberius -David (641)
Table data.Succession: Son of Heraclius; co-emperor since 4 July 638. Co-ruler with Constantine and then sole emperor under the regency of his mother Martina
Table data.Life details: 626 – unknown Deposed, mutilated and exiled, subsequent fate unknown

Table data.Name: Constans II "the Bearded" Constantinus , Κωνσταντῖνος
Table data.Succession: Son of Heraclius Constantine; proclaimed co-emperor by Heraclonas at age 11
Table data.Life details: 7 November 630 – 15 July 668 (aged 37) Lost Egypt in 641. Murdered in Sicily while bathing by supporters of Mezezius

Table data.Name: Constantine IV "the Younger" Constantinus , Κωνσταντῖνος
Table data.Reign: September 668 – 10 July (?) 685 (16 years and 10 months) with his brothers Heraclius and Tiberius (659–681)
Table data.Succession: Son of Constans II; co-emperor since 13 April 654
Table data.Life details: Roughly 650 – 10 July (?) 685 (aged about 35) Defeated the First Arab Siege of Constantinople . Died of dysentery

Table data.Name: Justinian II "Rhinotmetus" Justinianus , Ἰουστινιανός
Table data.Succession: Son of Constantine IV, chosen as successor over Constans' sons
Table data.Life details: 668/669 – 4 November 711 (aged 42) Deposed and mutilated (hence his nickname, "Slit-nosed") by Leontius in 695; returned to the throne in 705

The municipal roads are the lowest level of roadway in the country, typically found in rural areas and marked as K with a number on a white field though it is not observed on the ground.

Table data.Succession: First king of unified Numidia after Syphax 's defeat, made his kingdom a huge regional power in North Africa.

Table data.Name: Micipsa
Table data.Succession: Inherited the throne with his two brother but outlived them by almost 30 years and reigned alone from then.
Table data.Life details: c. 198 – 118 (aged 80) Probably died of old age.

Table data.Name: Gulussa
Table data.Succession: Chosen as successor with his two brothers, great general and tactician. Nothing else known.
Table data.Life details: Unknown lifespan Cause of death unknown.

Table data.Name: Mastanabal
Table data.Succession: Chosen as successor with his two brothers. Won a gold medal at the Athens Hippodrome in a horse-drawn chariot racing event.
Table data.Life details: Unknown lifespan No mention of him after 139BC, most likely died of illness.

Table data.Name: Hiempsal I
Table data.Reign: c. 118 – c. 117 BCE (less than a year)
Table data.Succession: Son and successor of Micipsa with his brother Adherbal and his cousin Jugurtha .
Table data.Life details: ? – c. 117 BCE (age unknown) Murdered with his supporters by Jugurtha 's men.

Table data.Name: Adherbal
Table data.Succession: Son and successor of Micipsa with his brother Hiempsal I and his cousin Jugurtha .
Table data.Life details: ? – c. 112 BCE (age unknown) Besieged and murdered by Jugurtha despite being put under protection by the Romans.

Table data.Name: Jugurtha
Table data.Succession: Son of Mastanabal , overthrew and killed all of his rivals resulting in a war with Rome.
Table data.Life details: c. 160 – 104 BCE (aged 56) Defeated and captured by the Romans then thrown into the Tullianum prison, where he was executed by strangulation .

Table data.Name: Massiva II
Table data.Succession: Fled to Rome after his cousin's murder where he claimed the Numidian throne and probably was chosen as a rival king by the Roman Senate.
Table data.Life details: ? – 110 BC (age unknown) Murdered by Jugurtha's men in Rome .

Table data.Name: Gauda
Table data.Succession: Brother of Jugurtha , placed as king by the romans after his brother's defeat. Last king of unified Numidia.
Table data.Life details: ? – 88 BCE (age unknown) Died of unknown causes.
